findings.title: Renewal cleanup can remain permanently blocked after a later conclusive observation
findings.rationale: The proposed guard correctly routes malformed successful observations into the existing completePairing catch. At channels.service.ts:168–171, that catch preserves the prior cleanup identity and sets the current attempt to ERROR/CLEANUP_AMBIGUOUS. A subsequent INITIAL can reconcile the detached prior identity through :47–67 and mark it CLEANED, but that branch neither clears the live channel's pendingCleanup tuple nor advances its attempt. The next INITIAL fails CHANNEL_SLOT_OCCUPIED because canResume at :93–96 excludes CLEANUP_AMBIGUOUS; RENEW fails CLEANUP_RECOVERY_REQUIRED at :97. Thus parser-only hardening preserves uncertainty but does not establish the proposal's promised recovery after valid absence/deletion. This is a static caller-transition finding, not an executed failure or a claim that the adapter introduced the underlying recovery defect. Existing lifecycle coverage exercises successful renewal cleanup and post-unlink ambiguity, but does not cover this retained-renewal error-to-recovery sequence.
findings.suggested_action: Explicitly include a fenced recovery transition in the proposal using already-admitted caller surfaces. Preserve the same reserved replacement, generation, pairing epoch and attempt; reconcile the exact prior cleanup tuple and reach RESERVED_NEVER_CREATED before permitting its single create. Require the actual-adapter lifecycle regression to continue beyond CLEANUP_COMPLETED_RETRY_PAIR and prove successful explicit recovery, rather than stopping at safe refusal or a cleaned tombstone.

findings.title: Added unit cases do not protect independent validation and compatibility branches
findings.rationale: The proposed.diff cases meaningfully detect the original non-array/invalid-JSON defect, a null row, malformed ownerJid and duplicate target names. However, removing the new name validation or the connectionStatus validation would still leave every proposed case passing. For example, [{name:'another-instance',connectionStatus:7}] would again become conclusive absence if that independent check regressed. The positive matching case supplies both optional fields, so preservation of null projection for a matching row with missing or null optional fields is also unproved.
findings.suggested_action: Extend the proposed table with missing/non-string/blank names and malformed connectionStatus, and add matching-row cases with omitted and null optional fields. Retain valid nonmatching absence, unique matching projection, duplicate rejection, one-request assertions and every existing test. These remain bounded adapter tests; they supplement the required actual-adapter product-path regression.

findings.title: Product-path wording contradicts the preserved absence contract
findings.rationale: The proposal's required_product_path_regression_case_if_accepted calls this an 'Instagram create/renew pairing flow' and later describes valid [] as the 'only absence case'. The actual flow is WhatsApp/Evolution pairing exercised by the Instagram lifecycle regression spec. The proposal's own behavior definition and diff correctly preserve valid nonmatching inventories as absence too. The root clarification resolves the intended subject, but the frozen proposal still contains both misleading statements.
findings.suggested_action: Name the WhatsApp/Evolution pairing/renewal flow explicitly. State that conclusive absence requires a fully validated inventory without the exact target, including [] and valid nonmatching rows. Make coverage of both currently reachable cleanup paths explicit rather than conditional.
